summary: Shechting a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash and offering it up outside are two separate sins. Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says one who shechted it outside is not punished for then offering it outside, since it was already pasul; the Sages disagree.

chunks.en: One who shechts and offers up outside,
chunks.st: One who slaughters an offering outside the Temple courtyard and one who offers it up outside

words.note: Outside the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: חַיָּב עַל הַשְּׁחִיטָה וְחַיָּב עַל הָעֲלִיָּה.
chunks.en: is liable for the shechting and liable for the offering up.
chunks.st: the Temple courtyard is liable for the slaughter and liable for the offering up,
chunks.stMore: as each act involves an independent prohibition. If done intentionally, he is liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet] for each act, and if done unwittingly, he is liable to bring a sin offering for each act.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: if he shechted inside and offered up outside,
chunks.st: If he slaughtered an offering inside the courtyard and then offered it up outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. If he shechted outside and offered up outside,
chunks.st: he is liable. But if he slaughtered it outside, thereby rendering it unfit, and then he offered it up outside,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלָה בַחוּץ אֶלָּא דָבָר פָּסוּל.
chunks.en: he is free, because he offered up outside only a pasul thing.
chunks.st: he is exempt for the offering up, as he offered up only an item that is unfit,
chunks.stMore: and one is liable only for offering up an item that is fit to be offered up inside the Temple.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: even one who shechts inside and offers up outside,
chunks.st: According to your reasoning, even in a case where he slaughters it inside and offers it up outside, he should be exempt,

chunks.en: once he took it out, he made it pasul.
chunks.st: since the moment that he took it outside the courtyard, he thereby rendered it unfit.
chunks.stMore: Yet, in such a case, he is certainly liable for offering it up. So too, one who slaughters an offering outside and then offers it up outside is liable.

summary: A tamei person who eats korban meat is punished, whether the meat is tamei or tahor. Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says not if the meat was tamei, but the Sages say his own touch makes it tamei anyway. A tahor person who eats tamei meat is not punished with kares.

chunks.en: A tamei person who ate,
chunks.st: One who is ritually impure who ate sacrificial food,

chunks.he: בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָמֵא וּבֵין קֹדֶשׁ טָהוֹר,
chunks.en: whether tamei korban meat or tahor korban meat,
chunks.st: whether it was ritually impure sacrificial food or ritually pure sacrificial food,

chunks.en: is liable. Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says,
chunks.st: is liable to receive karet if he did so intentionally and to bring a sliding-scale offering if he did so unwittingly. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: a tamei person who ate tahor meat
chunks.st: An impure person who ate pure

chunks.en: is liable. But a tamei person who ate tamei meat
chunks.st: sacrificial food is liable. But an impure person who ate impure

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, שֶׁלֹּא אָכַל אֶלָּא דָבָר טָמֵא.
chunks.en: is free, because he ate only a tamei thing.
chunks.st: sacrificial food is exempt, as he merely ate an impure item,
chunks.stMore: and the prohibition against eating sacrificial food while one is impure applies only to pure sacrificial food.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: even a tamei person who ate tahor meat,
chunks.st: According to your logic, this halakha would apply even in a case of an impure person who ate what had been pure sacrificial food,

chunks.en: once he touched it,
chunks.st: because once he touched it, he

chunks.en: he made it tamei. And a tahor person who ate tamei meat
chunks.st: thereby rendered it ritually impure. Yet, in such a case, he is certainly liable for eating it. So too, an impure person who ate impure sacrificial food is liable. And a pure person who ate impure

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל טֻמְאַת הַגּוּף:
chunks.en: is free, because he is liable only for the tumah of his body.
chunks.st: sacrificial food is exempt, as one is liable for eating sacrificial food in impurity only due to the impurity of one’s body, but not due to the impurity of the food.

summary: Shechting outside is stricter in one way and offering up outside is stricter in another. Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yosei argue whether someone who offers up many times is punished each time, and whether he must offer it on a mizbeach.

chunks.en: Shechting is stricter than offering up in one way,
chunks.st: There is a greater stringency with regard to slaughtering outside the Temple courtyard than with regard to offering up outside,

chunks.en: and offering up is stricter than shechting in another.
chunks.st: and there is a greater stringency with regard to offering up outside than with regard to slaughtering outside. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: Shechting is stricter:
chunks.st: The greater stringency with regard to slaughtering

chunks.en: one who shechts for a regular purpose
chunks.st: outside is that one who slaughters an offering outside the Temple courtyard even for the sake of an ordinary purpose, not for the sake of God,

words.note: For his own use, not for Hashem.

chunks.en: is liable, but one who offers up for a regular purpose
chunks.st: is liable. But one who offers up an offering outside the courtyard for the sake of an ordinary

chunks.en: is free. Offering up is stricter:
chunks.st: purpose is exempt. The greater stringency with regard to offering up

chunks.en: if two people held a knife and shechted,
chunks.st: outside is that two people who grasped a knife and together slaughtered

chunks.en: they are free. If they held a part and offered it up,
chunks.st: an offering outside the courtyard are exempt. But if two grasped a limb from an offering and together offered it up outside,

chunks.en: they are liable. If he offered up,
chunks.st: they are liable. If one unwittingly offered up

chunks.en: and offered up again,
chunks.st: part of an offering outside the courtyard and then in a different lapse of awareness offered up

chunks.en: and offered up again,
chunks.st: other parts of that offering and then again, in another lapse of awareness, offered up yet other parts,

chunks.en: he is liable for each and every offering up,
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering for each act of offering up;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Shimon.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: he is liable only once,
chunks.st: He is liable to bring only one sin offering.

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
chunks.en: and he is not liable until he offers it up on top of a mizbeach.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei adds: And one is liable for offering up an offering outside the courtyard only once he offers it up at the top of an altar that was erected there.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even if he offered it up on a rock
chunks.st: Even if he offered it up on a rock

chunks.en: or on a stone, he is liable.
chunks.st: or on a stone, not an altar, he is liable.

summary: One who offers outside a kosher korban, or one that became pasul in the Beis HaMikdash, is liable, even for an olive-size. Rabbi Elazar says that for things like the kometz and levonah he is liable only if he offered all of it outside.

chunks.en: Both kosher korbanos and korbanos
chunks.st: With regard to both fit sacrificial animals, and

chunks.en: that became pasul in the holy place,
chunks.st: unfit sacrificial animals whose disqualification occurred in sanctity, i.e., in the course of the Temple service,

chunks.en: if he offered them outside,
chunks.st: and one sacrificed them outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. One who offers up an olive-size of the olah
chunks.st: he is liable. One who offers up outside the courtyard an olive-bulk made up of the flesh of a burnt offering and of

chunks.en: and of the fats outside,
chunks.st: its sacrificial portions

chunks.en: is liable. The kometz,
chunks.st: is liable.
chunks.stMore: If there is a meal offering from which a handful was not removed, and one sacrificed it outside the Temple courtyard, he is exempt from liability, because until the handful is actually removed it is not fit to be burned on the altar inside the Temple. But if a priest took a handful from it and then returned its handful into the remainder of the meal offering, and one sacrificed the entire mixture outside the courtyard, he is liable, as once the handful has been removed it is fit to be burned on the altar inside the Temple, and one is liable for offering it up outside even though it is mixed into the remainder. With regard to the handful of a meal offering,

chunks.st: the frankincense, the incense,

chunks.en: the mincha of Kohanim,
chunks.st: the meal offering of priests,

chunks.en: and the mincha of the nesachim,
chunks.st: and the meal offering brought with the libations that accompany animal offerings,

chunks.en: if he offered an olive-size of one of them outside,
chunks.st: in a case where one sacrificed even an olive-bulk from any one of these, which should be sacrificed on the altar, outside the Temple,

chunks.en: he is liable. Rabbi Elazar says he is free
chunks.st: he is liable, as the burning of an olive-bulk is considered a proper burning. Rabbi Eliezer deems him exempt

chunks.en: until he offers all of it.
chunks.st: unless he sacrifices the whole of any one of these items outside the Temple.

chunks.en: And all of them that he offered inside but left
chunks.st: But Rabbi Eliezer concedes that with regard to any of them that one sacrificed inside

chunks.en: an olive-size of them, and offered it outside,
chunks.st: the courtyard but left over an olive-bulk from them and then sacrificed that olive-bulk outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. And all of them that were missing any amount,
chunks.st: he is liable. And with regard to any of these offerings that were lacking any amount,

chunks.en: and he offered them outside, he is free.
chunks.st: if one sacrifices it outside the courtyard, he is exempt.

summary: One who offers korban meat and its fats outside is liable for the fats. A mincha whose kometz was not yet taken is not punished when offered outside, but once the kometz was taken, it is.

chunks.en: One who offers korbanos and their fats outside,
chunks.st: One who sacrifices sacrificial meat, which is eaten, and sacrificial portions, i.e., those that are to be burned on the altar, outside the courtyard,

words.en: and their parts for the mizbeach

chunks.he: חַיָּב. מִנְחָה שֶׁלֹּא נִקְמְצָה וְהִקְרִיבָהּ בַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: is liable. A mincha whose kometz was not taken, if he offered it outside,
chunks.st: is liable for the sacrifice of the sacrificial portions. But he is not liable for sacrificing the meat. If there is a meal offering from which a handful was not removed, and one sacrificed it outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: he is free. If he took its kometz,
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability, because until the handful is actually removed it is not fit to be burned on the altar inside the Temple. But if a priest took a handful from it and

chunks.en: and put the kometz back into it,
chunks.st: then returned its handful into the remainder of the meal offering,

chunks.en: and offered it outside, he is liable.
chunks.st: and one sacrificed the entire mixture outside the courtyard, he is liable,
chunks.stMore: as once the handful has been removed it is fit to be burned on the altar inside the Temple, and one is liable for offering it up outside even though it is mixed into the remainder.

summary: One who offers outside only the kometz or only the levonah is liable; Rabbi Elazar says only if he offers the second too. The same is true for the two bowls of levonah of the lechem hapanim. Sprinkling some of the blood outside also makes one liable.
stIntro: The burning of both the handful and the frankincense permits the consumption of the remainder of the meal offering by the priests.

chunks.en: The kometz and the levonah,
chunks.st: With regard to the handful and the frankincense,

chunks.en: if he offered one of them outside,
chunks.st: in a case where one sacrificed only one of them outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. Rabbi Elazar says he is free until
chunks.st: he is liable. Rabbi Eliezer exempts

chunks.en: he offers the second one too.
chunks.st: from liability one who burns only one of them until he also sacrifices the second.
chunks.stMore: Since the remainder of the meal offering becomes permitted only once both have been burned, he considers each one alone to be an incomplete offering, and he holds one is not liable for sacrificing only one of them.

chunks.en: One inside and one outside,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer concedes that if one sacrificed one inside the courtyard and one outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. Two bowls of levonah,
chunks.st: he is liable. The burning of two bowls of frankincense permits the consumption of the shewbread. With regard to the two bowls of frankincense,

chunks.en: if he offered one of them outside,
chunks.st: in a case where one sacrificed only one of them outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. Rabbi Elazar says he is free,
chunks.st: he is liable. Rabbi Eliezer exempts

chunks.st: from liability one who burns only one of them until he also sacrifices the second,

chunks.en: he is liable. One who throws some of the blood outside
chunks.st: he is liable. One who sprinkles part of the blood of an offering, e.g., one sprinkling instead of four, outside

chunks.en: is liable. Rabbi Elazar says,

chunks.he: אַף הַמְנַסֵּךְ מֵי חָג בֶּחָג בַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: even one who pours the water of Sukkos on Sukkos outside

chunks.en: is liable. Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: is liable. Rabbi Neḥemya says:

chunks.en: the leftover blood that he offered outside, he is liable.
chunks.st: For the remainder of the blood of an offering that was supposed to be poured at the base of the altar and that instead one sacrificed outside the courtyard, one is liable.

summary: A bird korban that had melikah inside and was offered outside makes one liable, but not if the melikah was outside. With shechitah it is the other way around. Rabbi Shimon disagrees about a bird shechted inside.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹלֵק אֶת הָעוֹף בִּפְנִים וְהֶעֱלָה בַחוּץ,
chunks.en: One who does melikah on a bird inside and offers it up outside,
chunks.st: One who pinches the nape of a bird offering inside the Temple courtyard and then offers it up outside

chunks.en: is liable. If he did melikah outside and offered it up outside,
chunks.st: the courtyard is liable. But if one pinched its nape outside the courtyard and then offered it up outside

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הָעוֹף בִּפְנִים וְהֶעֱלָה בַחוּץ,
chunks.en: he is free. One who shechts a bird inside and offers it up outside,
chunks.st: the courtyard he is exempt, as pinching the nape of a bird outside the courtyard is not considered valid pinching. One who slaughters, with a knife, a bird offering inside the courtyard and offers it up outside

chunks.en: is free. If he shechted it outside and offered it up outside,
chunks.st: the courtyard is exempt, as slaughtering a bird offering in the Temple courtyard disqualifies it as an offering. But if one slaughtered a bird offering outside the courtyard and then offered it up outside,

chunks.en: he is liable. So we find,
chunks.st: he is liable. Evidently,

chunks.en: the way it is made kosher inside
chunks.st: the manner of its preparation inside the courtyard, i.e., pinching,

chunks.en: makes him free outside,
chunks.st: effects its exemption outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: and the way it is made kosher outside
chunks.st: and the manner of its preparation outside the courtyard, i.e., slaughter,

chunks.en: makes him free inside.
chunks.st: effects its exemption inside the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: anything that one is liable for outside,
chunks.st: With regard to any act of killing an animal concerning which, when it was performed outside the courtyard, one is liable for subsequently offering it up outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: one is liable for the same done inside
chunks.st: one is also liable for

chunks.en: that he then offered up outside,
chunks.st: having offered the animal up outside the courtyard after performing a similar act of killing inside the courtyard.

chunks.he: חוּץ מִן הַשּׁוֹחֵט בִּפְנִים וּמַעֲלֶה בַחוּץ:
chunks.en: except for one who shechts inside and offers up outside.
chunks.st: This is the halakha except with regard to one who slaughters a bird inside the courtyard and offers it up outside the courtyard; he is exempt.

summary: If chatas blood was put both outside and inside, one is liable for the outside putting. Two chatas animals, where one was lost and found again, follow the same rule: whichever is done outside first makes him liable, and the inside one brings kapparah.

chunks.en: A chatas whose blood he caught in one cup,
chunks.st: With regard to a sin offering where one collected its blood in one cup,

chunks.en: if he put some outside and then put some inside,
chunks.st: if he first placed its blood on an altar outside the courtyard and then placed the remaining blood on the altar inside the courtyard,

chunks.en: or inside and then put some outside,
chunks.st: or if he first placed its blood on the altar inside the courtyard and then placed the remaining blood on an altar outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable, because all of it is fit to go inside.
chunks.st: in both cases he is liable for placing the blood outside the courtyard, as the blood in its entirety is fit to be placed on the altar inside the courtyard.

chunks.en: If he caught its blood in two cups,
chunks.st: If one collected its blood in two cups

chunks.en: and put both of them inside,
chunks.st: and placed the blood from both of them on the altar inside

chunks.en: he is free. Both of them outside,
chunks.st: the courtyard he is exempt as he acted appropriately. If he placed the blood from both of them on an altar outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. One inside and one outside,
chunks.st: he is liable, as both are fit to be placed inside. If he first placed the blood from one cup inside and then placed the blood from the other one outside,

chunks.en: he is free. One outside and one inside,
chunks.st: he is exempt. By using the blood of the first cup to perform the mitzva of placing the blood on the altar, he thereby rendered the blood in the second cup unfit to be placed on the altar; therefore, there is no liability for placing it on an altar outside. If he first placed the blood from one cup outside and then placed the blood from the other one inside,

chunks.en: he is liable for the outside one,
chunks.st: he is liable for the external placement as that blood was fit to be placed inside,

chunks.en: and the inside one brings kapparah.
chunks.st: and the internal placement atones
chunks.stMore: for the transgression for which the sin offering was brought.

chunks.en: What is this like?
chunks.st: To what is this matter comparable?

chunks.en: and now both of them are standing there.
chunks.st: In that case, both of them stand before him and he must sacrifice one as his sin offering.

chunks.en: If he shechted both of them inside,
chunks.st: If he slaughtered both of them inside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is free. If he shechted both of them outside,
chunks.st: he is exempt. If he slaughtered both of them outside the courtyard,

chunks.en: he is liable. One inside and one outside,
chunks.st: he is liable, as each was fit to be slaughtered in the courtyard. If he first slaughtered one inside and then slaughtered the other one outside

chunks.en: he is free. One outside and one inside,
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability for slaughtering the second, as he has already fulfilled his obligation with the first, thereby rendering the second one unfit for sacrifice. If he first slaughtered one outside and then slaughtered the other one inside

chunks.en: he is liable for the outside one,
chunks.st: he is liable for slaughtering the external
chunks.stMore: animal outside the courtyard, as it was fit to be slaughtered inside,

chunks.en: and the inside one brings kapparah.
chunks.st: and the internal animal atones
chunks.stMore: for the transgression for which the sin offering was brought. The mishna adds: In a case where one slaughtered both inside the courtyard,

chunks.en: Just as its blood frees its own meat,
chunks.st: just as placing the blood of the first animal exempts one who consumes its meat from liability for misuse of consecrated property,

chunks.he: כָּךְ הוּא פוֹטֵר אֶת בְּשַׂר חֲבֶרְתָּהּ:
